issues: whether a commercial business that leaves a vehicle unlocked with keys in a lot owes a duty of care to a third party injured when the vehicle is stolen and crashed
the standard of care owed by a commercial business in securing vehicles on its premises
whether theft of an unlocked vehicle by a young person is a foreseeable risk giving rise to a duty
whether the criminal act of a third party (theft) constitutes a novus actus interveniens that severs the chain of causation
whether the passenger's decision to ride in a stolen vehicle amounts to contributory negligence reducing recovery
whether the passenger's voluntary assumption of risk (volenti non fit injuria) bars or limits recovery
heads of damages available for personal injury in a negligence action
key_facts: vehicle was unlocked with keys in it
vehicle was in a commercial garage lot
the claim is against the business, not the driver
needs_clarification: Which province or territory does this scenario arise in? Tort law (duty of care, standard of care, defences, damages) is governed by provincial common law and provincial Negligence Acts, and the applicable authorities will differ by jurisdiction.
